book.pastel.guidebook.boogaloo.cutting_b: I put this one together on a Cutting Board.
I put these together on a Cutting Board.
book.pastel.guidebook.boogaloo.effect.ni: Soothes the mind and slows a racing heart.
book.pastel.guidebook.boogaloo.effect.bo: A poison that does not stop at half a heart.
book.pastel.guidebook.boogaloo.effect.ja: A sleep that grows heavier the longer it lasts.
book.pastel.guidebook.boogaloo.effect.ev: Sleep so deep it may never end. Handle with respect.
book.pastel.guidebook.boogaloo.effect.ja: Shrugs off harmful effects while it lasts.
book.pastel.guidebook.boogaloo.effect.do: Saps vitality and stops natural healing.
book.pastel.guidebook.boogaloo.effect.ci: Keeps hunger at bay with gentle warmth.
book.pastel.guidebook.boogaloo.effect.dr: Old wounds reopen; healing is weakened.
book.pastel.guidebook.boogaloo.effect.ne: A creeping drowsiness that dulls the senses.
book.pastel.guidebook.boogaloo.witches_b:
I spent weeks on a Potion Workshop of my own design, and then I watched a witch do the same work with a cauldron, a fire and a lot less fuss.\
\
I've packed the Workshop away. My potions are brewed the witches' way now, and the effects I discovered still work. Each one just needs the right Pastel ingredient dropped into the brew.

The trinkets and blades I used to infuse in the Workshop can be steeped in a ritual circle instead. Place the item, the ingredient for the effect I want, and a Whiff of Magic inside the chalk, then begin the rite.\
\
For a blade or oils, adding Glowstone Dust gives level II and a Midnight Chip level III, but the effect wears off sooner. Steeping a blade again only swaps its effect. Its enchantments stay.\
\
See [Lesser Potion Pendant](entry://brewing/lesser_potion_pendant) and [Nightfall's Blade](entry://equipment/tools_and_armor/nightfalls_blade).
book.pastel.guidebook.lesser_potion_pend:
Potions are handy. Carrying half an inventory of them around, however, is not.\
The Potion Pendant has a small chamber that holds one effect. As long as I wear it and have Ink on me, I keep receiving that effect.
book.pastel.guidebook.boogaloo.pendant.f:
To fill a pendant, I place it in a small ritual circle with a Whiff of Magic and one ingredient:\
\
- Sugar: Speed\
- Prismarine Crystals: Haste\
- Blaze Powder: Strength\
- Rabbit's Foot: Jump Boost\
- Golden Carrot: Night Vision\
- Ghast Tear: Regeneration\
- Magma Cream: Fire Resistance\
- Kelp: Water Breathing\
- Turtle Scute: Resistance\
- Golden Apple: Absorption\
- Phantom Membrane: Slow Falling\
- Citrine Shard: Nourishing\
- Peach: Toughness\
- Nightdew Sprout: Calming\
- Jade Jelly: Immunity\
book.pastel.guidebook.boogaloo.pendant.c: Brewed in a witch's cauldron, with a Block of Uranium to hold the shape.
book.pastel.guidebook.greater_potion_pen:
Works very much like its [little brother](entry://brewing/lesser_potion_pendant), but has three chambers. Each holds a level I effect.\
\
I've settled on four blends that work well together, each steeped in a large ritual circle with Breath of the Goddess.
book.pastel.guidebook.boogaloo.greater.e: Explorer: Speed, Night Vision and Water Breathing.
book.pastel.guidebook.boogaloo.greater.m: Miner: Haste, Night Vision and Fire Resistance.
book.pastel.guidebook.boogaloo.greater.c: Three pieces of Polished Antimetal give it its three chambers.
book.pastel.guidebook.use_in_potion_work:
Steep it in a small ritual circle with a Whiff of Magic and the ingredient of a harmful effect: Spider Eye, Fermented Spider Eye, Wither Rose, Bone Ash, Downstone Fragments or Dragonbone Chunk.\
\
The stored effect gets reapplied every 15 seconds.
book.pastel.guidebook.boogaloo.remembran:
I had plans for a Spirit Instiller: a machine to bind the energies of two items with a third. A witch showed me her chalk circles and I tore up the blueprints.\
\
Everything I meant to build it for is done better by ritual, or in my [Fusion Shrine](entry://general/fusion_shrine).

- Creatures: a head, the creature's favourite item and Vegetal in a ritual circle make a Memory of it. See [Memories](entry://creating_life/memories).\
- Idols: crafted in a ritual circle. See [Idols](entry://creating_life/idols).\
- Jade Vine Bulbs, Blood Orchids, Budding Onyx and the Nectar Lance: fused in the Fusion Shrine with Liquid Crystal.\
- Spawners: tuned in a ritual circle. See [Spawner Manipulation](entry://creating_life/spawner_manipulation).
book.pastel.guidebook.memories.page0.tex:
With a witch's chalk circle I can breathe new life into a creature that is long gone.\
\
The rite doesn't bring it back right away. It leaves an ethereal echo of the creature, which I called a *Memory*. I can carry it around and place it wherever I want the creature to wake up.
The mightiest creatures resist. Recalling an Elder Guardian, Warden, Wither or Ender Dragon takes a far larger circle, Infernal Chalk, Ectoplasm and an altar of real power.\
\
The circle won't hold one until I've seen a smaller Memory manifest. Before that it just spits my offerings back out.\
\
Creatures from farther away can be remembered too, with a skull or something they drop in place of the head. The big ones won't come back for me until I've killed one myself.\
\
*I should probably not do this next to my house.*
book.pastel.guidebook.spawner_manipulati:
With [Resonance](entry://enchanting/enchantments/resonance) on my pickaxe, Spawners finally drop, and they keep the creature they had in them.\
\
A chalk circle can tune them. The Spawner has to sit flush with the floor, with the Golden Chalk drawn right on top of it.\
*This gon be gud.*
book.pastel.guidebook.boogaloo.spawner.s:
If the circle finds no Spawner under the Golden Chalk, or the Spawner can't be pushed any further, it gives the offerings back. The altar's power is spent either way.\
\
A dungeon Spawner can be done where it stands once I raise the floor around it.\
\
Spawners keep spawning while I work. Some light around the circle helps.
book.pastel.guidebook.spawner_manipulati: Each rite adds one more creature per spawn, up to 8.
Each rite makes the Spawner a little quicker, down to one wave every 5 to 10 seconds.

Spawners seem to naturally stop spawning creatures when there are a lot of them around. Almost as if they want to give me a chance. *Pathetic, isn't it? As if I needed that.*\
Each rite lets two more creatures crowd around it, up to 16.
Each rite lets me stand 4 blocks further away and keep it running, up to 32.
book.pastel.guidebook.spawner_creature_c:
The circle takes a Memory and pours it into the Spawner below. Whatever the Spawner held before is forgotten. Colours and markings carry over.\
\
The creature still needs the right ground and light to appear, so a cow Spawner wants grass.\
\
The greatest creatures won't be bound this way.
book.pastel.guidebook.jade_vines.page1.t:
Once almost a lost cause, I now have an ace up my sleeve:\
Fused in my [Fusion Shrine](entry://general/fusion_shrine) with Liquid Crystal and plenty of Vegetal, I'm sure the little deadish bulb will wake up again.
book.pastel.guidebook.idols.page0.text:
Manifestations of a creature in block form, shaped in a ritual circle from its head, Vegetal, Radium Shards and Stardust.\
\
Using them, walking on them, or hitting them with a projectile triggers an action specifically associated with that creature.
I will have to create the 'blackest of blacks' in the [Fusion Shrine](entry://general/fusion_shrine) in a way that absolutely no unregulated light can contaminate the crystal. *So midnight it is*!\
\
Best to bring a [](item://minecraft:clock) with me. A witch's Set Midnight rite works too, if I'm impatient.
book.pastel.guidebook.celestial_pocketwa: The problem with [Onyx Shards](entry://general/onyx_shards) is that their creation is tied to midnight. And, of course, every time I look at the clock, the window of time seems to have just passed by. This pocketwatch lets me nudge time along.
book.pastel.guidebook.bedrock_armor.page:
The strongest armor I knew was the Ultimate set the ants' researchers forged from uranium and titanium. But even it wears down.\
\
Fused in Midnight Solution with Bedrock Dust, an Ultimate piece becomes something that simply *cannot* be damaged. And it's stronger, too.
Every piece comes with Protection, Fire, Blast and Projectile Protection V. This one adds Respiration III and Aqua Affinity.
Every piece comes with Protection, Fire, Blast and Projectile Protection V. This one adds Inexorable.
Every piece comes with Protection, Fire, Blast and Projectile Protection V. This one adds Swift Sneak III.
Every piece comes with Protection, Fire, Blast and Projectile Protection V. This one adds Feather Falling IV and Depth Strider III.
book.pastel.guidebook.jadeite.page0.text: Imposing vines hang from the high ceiling, breaking the darkness with their light. Their petals are a key ingredient for Eternal Slumber in a witch's brew.
book.pastel.guidebook.jadeite.page1.text: They are very tasty, and their petals can be brewed into Eternal Slumber in a witch's cauldron.
book.pastel.guidebook.sawblade_holly.pag:
Harvested by shearing a Sawblade Holly Bush. Used in cooking.\
\
*Clearly easier to digest cooked than raw...*
book.pastel.guidebook.nightfalls_blade.p:
This small blade is too fine to inflict serious wounds, but has many sharp thorns that will bore into my opponent's flesh.\
\
When steeped in a ritual circle with a harmful ingredient, a struck opponent will be afflicted with the effect, as long as I carry Ink of its color. Glowstone Dust in the circle raises it to level II and a Midnight Chip to level III, at the cost of a shorter effect.\
\
I can steep it again whenever I want a different effect. The old one is washed out, and the blade keeps its enchantments.
book.pastel.guidebook.budding_onyx.page0:
Crafting [Onyx](entry://general/onyx_shards) was always tricky, as it only works at midnight. I kept missing that short window.
Making Onyx growable like the other gems will save me a lot of time.

*Strangely, the same procedure doesn't seem to work for the others?*
advancements.pastel.build_spirit_instill: Craft Golden Chalk and learn to bind spirits in a witch's ritual circle
Craft a Potion Pendant in a witch's cauldron and steep it in a ritual circle
book.pastel.guidebook.boogaloo.antimetal:
A pale metal from Thoraxis that wants nothing to do with the ground. The ants' researchers call it Antimetal; I call it the most useful thing I've ever pried out of a wall.\
\
Where my old notes call for a light, floaty material, this is it. Polished Antimetal stands in wherever I need a whole, flawless piece.
book.pastel.guidebook.paltaeria.page2.te: Packed tightly enough, Antimetal stops pretending to be a block and starts trying to leave. It would not be a good idea to place this outdoors - my future self will thank me.
book.pastel.guidebook.boogaloo.antimetal: The ant worlds hide a metal that doesn't respect gravity.
Antimetal comes from Thoraxis. Polish it to get the flawless pieces some recipes ask for.
book.pastel.guidebook.storm_stones.page0:
Storms are a powerful manifestation of Mother Nature.\
Using the [Fusion Shrine](entry://general/fusion_shrine) I even started one while I was crafting [some powerful resources](entry://general/onyx_shards).\
\
There is no doubt that I will find something related to them that can help me on my journey.
book.pastel.guidebook.boogaloo.vortex.pa:
Out in Thoraxis's Vortex Expanse, the wind itself takes shape. Its Vortexes leave behind these charges, humming with bottled storm.\
Used in the [Fusion Shrine](entry://general/fusion_shrine), I can summon a thunderstorm with ease.
book.pastel.guidebook.boogaloo.vortex.hi: Somewhere in the ant worlds, storms have learned to walk.
Vortexes roam Thoraxis's Vortex Expanse. Defeat them for Vortex Charges.
book.pastel.guidebook.treasure_hunter.pa:
Then I remembered the Creepers! After being struck by lightning, they explode with such force that they blow their enemies' heads right off their necks (worst case: mine).\
To replicate this, I came up with an enchantment using [Vortex Charges](entry://general/storm_stones).\
And so Treasure Hunter was born, allowing me to collect [all kinds of Mob Heads](entry://creating_life/mob_heads).
book.pastel.guidebook.boogaloo.blood_cry:
Crimson spires grow out of the Lucid Pools in Thoraxis, shining in stunning scarlet and bleeding with willful magic.\
\
The shards carry the same fierce energy I once tried to coax out of Kindling feathers, only far more of it.
book.pastel.guidebook.resplendent_feathe:
The rather resplendent feathers of [Kindlings](entry://creating_life/kindlings) are quite remarkable, so much so that I'm forced to give the little bumpkins coat trimmings on a regular basis.\
The drops of blood that come with them remind me of the [Blood Crystal](entry://creating_life/bloodstone) spires in Thoraxis.
book.pastel.guidebook.draconic_twinsword:
What my musings have created here is nothing short of a masterpiece of versatility.\
This double-headed sword is exquisitely balanced, allowing for wide and powerful sweeping attacks. The delicate [Blood Crystal](entry://creating_life/bloodstone) construction of the weapon makes it delightfully stalwart, and excellent at keeping an edge.\
\
An unwelcoming, yet entrancing weapon.
book.pastel.guidebook.boogaloo.azurite.b: Thoraxis Bluestone turns out to be a close cousin of Bluestone. Fused with Lapis and Blue Pigment, it settles into Raw Bluestone.
book.pastel.guidebook.boogaloo.azurite.g: Bluestone also works as a starter in the Crystallarieum.
book.pastel.guidebook.malachite_tools.pa:
Its sheer size allows me to hit enemies from a greater distance with ease.\
\
*If it weren't for the [Antimetal](entry://general/paltaeria), I probably wouldn't even be able to lift it.*
book.pastel.guidebook.hoverblock.page0.t: Created from a collision of [Uranium](entry://general/stratine) and [Antimetal](entry://general/paltaeria) floatblocks, this block just... floats around, vibing.
book.pastel.guidebook.boogaloo.tigers_ey: A warm amber gem that drinks in light and gives it back. The ants' world hides it in shrines and temples, but I've found a better way: Citrine fused with Amber Moss from Cavaryn's caves settles into Tiger's Eye right on my Pedestal.
Two Amber Moss, one Citrine Shard and a little yellow powder give me three gems. Plenty for the recipes that need real light energy.
For simple lamps and lights I don't need a gem at all. Glowcap Mushrooms from Cavaryn glow on their own, and they're everywhere down there.
Amber light lives deep in the ant world's caves.
Gather Amber Moss from the walls of Cavaryn's caves, thickest in the Glowcap Caves, then fuse it with Citrine on any Pedestal to make Tiger's Eye.
book.pastel.guidebook.shimmerstone_light:
On my first nights in this wonderful world, I used to light my improvised hut with torches. As atmospheric as that was, it was also primitive.\
To get away from my dark, torch-lit past, I created lamps based on glowing [Glowcap Mushrooms](entry://general/shimmerstone).
book.pastel.guidebook.gemstone_lights.pa:
When I set foot in the first geode, I was greeted by a pleasant, cozy glow.\
\
With the help of [Glowcap Mushrooms](entry://general/shimmerstone), it was easy to amplify this light to create fancy lights.
book.pastel.guidebook.radiant_glass.page:
I need a way to efficiently light my shelter and other structures. Pretty much the opposite of [#](bb00bb)Tinted Glass[#]()?\
\
What could be better than using the luminescent properties of [Glowcap](entry://general/shimmerstone)? The [Glowcap](entry://general/shimmerstone) used in its manufacture ensures that the glass glows from within.
book.pastel.guidebook.present.page0.text:
The people around me have helped me through some tough situations. It's about time I give something back. A dash of [Tiger's Eye](entry://general/shimmerstone) causes the package to explode in a colorful shower of particles.\
\
After I click the Present onto the items I want to gift, I have to wrap it and then set it down so the recipient can open it and I can watch them jump for joy.
book.pastel.guidebook.boogaloo.uranium.p:
Heavy, warm and humming. The ants' researchers mine Uranium out of Cavaryn's broodstone, and it is exactly the dense, stubborn material my recipes need. Where my old notes ask for something heavy, this is it.\
\
A full Block of Uranium stands in for a large, flawless piece.
book.pastel.guidebook.stratine.page2.tex:
Uranium is an exceptionally heavy material. Packed tightly, it pulls downward on everything around it.\
\
Shaping it with my [Pedestal](entry://general/pedestal) is no problem at all.
book.pastel.guidebook.boogaloo.uranium.h: The deepest ant caves are full of something heavy and warm.
Uranium ore grows in Cavaryn's broodstone. Any Uranium works for my recipes.
book.pastel.guidebook.boogaloo.radium.pa: The Toxic Caves that have crept into Cavaryn glow with Radium. Its shards carry the same sickly, potent energy my old swamp reeds used to, only far stronger.
The gas that pools in those caves can be bottled. A Bottle of Radon is where a recipe once asked for a whole reed.
book.pastel.guidebook.boogaloo.radium.hi: Something poisonous glows deep inside Cavaryn.
Find the Toxic Caves in Cavaryn. Mine Radium for its shards and bottle the Radon gas that collects there.
book.pastel.guidebook.boogaloo.broodfrui:
Molting vines in Cavaryn's Brooding Tunnels, Glowcap Caves and Wormy Caves bear these swollen fruit. Crack one and it's full of a clear, watery pulp, full of life and surprisingly eager to carry magic.\
\
It's become my go-to for anything that needs a strong bond with water, Liquid Crystal included.
Something sweet grows on the vines of the ant world's caves.
Look for molting vines in Cavaryn's Brooding Tunnels, Glowcap Caves and Wormy Caves and harvest their Broodfruit.
book.pastel.guidebook.mermaids_jam.page0:
*Tastes like the deep caves*\
\
A special kind of [Cheong](entry://cuisine/cheong) made from [Broodfruit](entry://general/mermaids_brush).
book.pastel.guidebook.mermaids_popcorn.p:
You know, the seeds inside Broodfruit are actually quite tasty. Of course I had to try them.\
I heated them up really strongly until the pressure from the inside caused them to burst all by themselves.\
\
*Crunchy*
book.pastel.guidebook.lagoon_rod.page0.t:
Spending quiet days on my patio I have noticed that marine life seems to be strangely attracted to the pulpy [Broodfruit](entry://general/mermaids_brush) I keep in my pockets. It floats surprisingly well, so I decided to use one as a bobber.\
\
Lo and behold, not only does it increase my success, but it also has a number of other interesting side effects...
book.pastel.guidebook.ashen_circlet.page:
The [Uranium](entry://general/stratine) I set in this circlet, itself a creation of the Nether, can absorb high temperatures with ease.\
It even protects me from the searing heat of Lava - if only for a short time.\
\
When combined with [#](449900)Fire Resistance[#](), I can swim in Lava almost as if it were Water.
book.pastel.guidebook.jeopardant.page0.t:
Adrenaline does not have to be the only thing racing through my veins in a state of emergency.\
\
With every heart lost, the [Uranium](entry://general/stratine) in this ring glows brighter and brighter, pulsing in sync with my racing heart - providing an exponential damage boost.
book.pastel.guidebook.failing.page0.text:
I'd be lying if I said that I wasn't gripped by ambition. These are my first big leaps towards changing the world, I can feel it!\
Empowered by the potent [Onyx](entry://general/onyx_shards)[#]() and [Uranium](entry://general/stratine), this second organism I have created is clearly... more active than the last creation.\
**And definitely hungrier.\
MUCH hungrier.**
book.pastel.guidebook.boogaloo.p4.grove:
In Elythia I found a whole grove of these trees, the **Prismatic Grove**. At first glance it's just an oak wood. Once I'd grown my first colored sapling, the whole grove lit up in every color at once.\
\
It's the best place I know to gather Pigment.
book.pastel.guidebook.boogaloo.p4.tuft: The colorful tufts that hang from Elythia's Truffalo trees hold pure color too. Crushed under an anvil, each one gives two Pigment of its color.
book.pastel.guidebook.boogaloo.p4.geodes:
The ant worlds have geodes too. I've found Topaz, Amethyst and Citrine geodes under Elythia's hills.\
\
Cavaryn and Thoraxis, strangely, have none.
book.pastel.guidebook.boogaloo.p4.amaran: Wild Amaranth grows in Elythia's meadows, Butterfly Fields, Truffalo Forests and the Prismatic Grove. Crushing a bushel gives me grains to plant at home.
book.pastel.guidebook.pedestal_customisa:
I can exchange the basalt blocks with calcite and choose the gemstone blocks as I like it best.\
\
The ant worlds' polished stone works too: Polished Shellstone, Myrmite, Broodstone and Nyxite all hold the focus, and a Polished Blood Crystal Block makes a fine gemstone block. Mixing them gives the structure my own personal touch.
I noticed that the notch seems to fit perfectly with a [Moonstone Core](entry://dimension/moonstone_cores).\
\
The clasp itself is jammed shut. Only something harder than the Locket can pry it open - a Kraken's tooth should do it.
Socketing [Malachite Tools](entry://dimension/malachite_tools) with [Moonstone Cores](entry://dimension/moonstone_cores) grants them powerful new abilities.\
\
The crest only holds when it's bound with a Nightmare Scale, taken from the Nightmare that haunts Thoraxis.
book.pastel.guidebook.boogaloo.p5.space:
Deep in the cellar, the Preservation Chest held something that didn't belong to this world at all: a stone of pure, deep blue that seemed to fold the space around it.\
\
Every traveller who finds their way here seems to find one waiting for them.
book.pastel.guidebook.concealing_oils.pa: This concoction caught my eye reading through the Poisoner's Handbook. I can use it to infuse food items with potion effects - I just have to steep it in a witch's ritual circle with a harmful ingredient first...
book.pastel.guidebook.dragonbone.page2.t: Only a [#](bb00bb)Witch's Oven[#]() gets hot enough to turn these bones to ash. With a Clay Jar in it, it even catches some of the fumes.
book.pastel.guidebook.dragonbone.page6.t: Most blocks can be smelted back to their polished form in an ordinary furnace.
book.pastel.guidebook.boogaloo.titration:
Not everything gets better with age. Cream, chocolate and the other plain foods taste the same after an hour as after a month, so I make those in a [#](bb00bb)Witch's Cauldron[#]() and keep the barrel for drinks.\
A few drinks can be rushed in the cauldron too. They come out young and weak, but they're fine for cooking.
book.pastel.guidebook.pure_resources.pag: Blasting these in a Blast Furnace gives a much more decent output.
advancements.pastel.tap_pure_alcohol.des: Distill a drink all the way down to Pure Alcohol
book.pastel.guidebook.nectar_gloves.page:
*These leave me wondering so many things.\
To bear dike while being devoid of [#](2432ff)Bluestone[#]()... how?*
book.pastel.guidebook.azure_dike_equipme:
- Grants [#](495b24)6[#]() units of [#](2c2e8e)Bluestone Dike[#]()
- Increases [#](2c2e8e)Bluestone Dike[#]() charging
book.pastel.guidebook.ideas.preservation: The entrance seems to be blocked by a powerful force field. However, whoever built it was kind enough to leave me some clues! The hearts on the sides of the force field indicate that I need to have [#](2c2e8e)Bluestone Dike[#]() active.
book.pastel.guidebook.azurite.page1.text:
Refining Bluestone is not a cheap task.\
In this refined form Bluestone can be used for many more recipes.
book.pastel.guidebook.azuresque_dike_cor:
My magnum opus of [#](2c2e8e)Bluestone Dike[#]()! The machinations of the preservation structures have puzzled me for so long, but I have finally made progress in replicating them!\
\
 Through the use of that... thing... I have managed to create a circuit that greatly empowers dike, speeding up its recovery and doubling any source of it.\
It is, however, unable to produce a shield on its own.
book.pastel.guidebook.pastel_network.pag:
[#](449900)Hoppers, Minecarts, Pipes[#](), and other such mundane methods of transport are nice, but *lacking*. These Bluestone-powered nodes - which I have named the [#](449900)Node Network[#]() - are a more elegant and much superior solution to the challenges of logistics.\
\
Due to reasons, the nodes are able to transfer items without line of sight. Another indicator of my natural genius!
text.autoconfig.pastel.option.AzureDikeH: Y Position of the Bluestone Dike Overlay on the players screen. Default: On top of Hearts
advancements.pastel.collect_azurite.desc: Collect Raw Bluestone. It has to be refined to be more useful
book.pastel.guidebook.puff_circlet.page0:
This glistening hoop creates a protective film of air around me.\
\
Grants [#](495b24)4[#]() units of [#](2c2e8e)Bluestone Dike[#](). Will protects me from projectiles and can cushion a long fall, using some of those charges.\
The Puff Circlet also prevents [#](bb00bb)Farmland[#]() from being trampled.
book.pastel.guidebook.azure_dike_equipme:
The results of combining [Bluestone](entry://general/azurite) with the protective properties of [Blue Pigment](entry://general/pigment@blue) really piqued my interest. The material seemed to surround itself with a transparent aura that took some effort to penetrate when I reached for the lump again.\
\
*This is going to be interesting...*
book.pastel.guidebook.azurite.page0.text: A rich blue crystal veining the Nyxite of Thoraxis. At a distance I almost mistook it for [Lapis](item://minecraft:lapis_lazuli) - were it not for the stunning aura that surrounded it.\n\nSeems to be able to intensify the energy of Pigment.
book.pastel.guidebook.azure_dike_equipme:
A magical aura surrounding my body, shielding me from incoming damage.\
Slowly but steadily recharges up to a certain amount.\
\
Each piece of [#](2c2e8e)Bluestone Dike[#]() equipment increases the maximum amount of protection.
text.autoconfig.pastel.option.AzureDikeH: Y Position of the Bluestone Dike Overlay on the players screen when not having full air. Default: On top of Armor
item.pastel.azure_dike_belt.tooltip: §7Greatly increases §9Bluestone Dike§7 recovery after getting hit
book.pastel.guidebook.azurite.name: Bluestone
book.pastel.guidebook.malachite.page0.te: A pristine material that sparkles in a deep green hue. It seems to have strong magical properties, almost like a abyssal analogue of [Bluestone](entry://general/azurite). In another similarity to [Bluestone](entry://general/azurite), Malachite also needs to be refined. I first have to grow the small fragments I found into full, usable crystals - though I'm not sure I'll see them fully grown in my lifetime, since I didn't find a budding block for them.
advancements.pastel.get_azure_dike_charg: Charge up a Point of Bluestone Dike by equipping a Trinket made out of Bluestone
book.pastel.guidebook.azure_dike_equipme:
- Grants [#](495b24)8[#]() units of [#](2c2e8e)Bluestone Dike[#]()
- Increases [#](2c2e8e)Bluestone Dike[#]() recovery after a hit, making it recharge quicker
book.pastel.guidebook.preservation_ruins: A powerful, magical force field. Wearing [Bluestone Dike equipment](entry://equipment/trinkets/azure_dike_equipment) allowed me to enter.
book.pastel.guidebook.azure_dike_equipme:
Infusing it with [Blue Ink](entry://ink/ink) in a [Color Picker](entry://ink/color_picker) increases the amount of [#](2c2e8e)Bluestone Dike[#]() provided.\
\
Cheap at first, but the required ink per level increases exponentially.
text.autoconfig.pastel.option.AzureDikeH: X Position of the Bluestone Dike Overlay on the players screen. Default: On top of Hearts
book.pastel.guidebook.nephrite.page1.tex:
Their blossoms are lovely, but the fruit they bear is brittle and inedible.\
For anything that calls for peaches I use [](item://antarchy:peach) from Elythia's Peach Forests instead. Eating one may give me a short burst of [Toughness](entry://brewing/effects/toughness).
book.pastel.guidebook.midnight_chip.page: The very drop I get from killing creatures with this feisty liquid enables me to make even more of it. Quite morbid, when I think about it.\nThe base is [#](bb00bb)Ichor[#](), the withering liquid that pools across Thoraxis. A chip and a little black pigment turn it to midnight.
book.pastel.guidebook.bedrock_tools.page:
Whenever I enter a new world I go about the mindless, days-long task of gathering villagers around me, turning them into zombies and healing them, only for one of them to eventually hand me a book of [#](449900)Mending[#](). All this just so I don't have to repair my tools.\
Now I take the finest tools I own, the [#](bb00bb)Ultimate[#]() ones, and fuse Bedrock into them. They come out unbreakable and stronger than before.\
Sneak-using the pickaxe, axe, shovel or hoe switches its mining area between 1x1, 3x3 and 5x5. The pickaxe and axe have one more setting that breaks every connected block of the same kind.
The Bedrock Pickaxe comes with **Efficiency VII**. Silk Touch or Fortune is my choice to add.
The Bedrock Axe comes with **Efficiency VII**.
The Bedrock Shovel comes with **Efficiency VII**.
The Bedrock Sword comes with **Sharpness VI**.
The Bedrock Hoe comes with **Efficiency VII**.
The Bedrock Bow comes with **Power VI**. Its arrows hit far harder than the Ultimate Bow's.
The Bedrock Crossbow comes with **Quick Charge IV**. Its bolts hit far harder than the Ultimate Crossbow's.
The Bedrock Shears come with **Efficiency VII**.
The Bedrock Fishing Rod comes with **Luck of the Sea IV**.
advancements.pastel.remember_egg_laying_: Shear, milk or feed an Egg Laying Wooly Pig. Some roam the meadows of Elythia

book.pastel.guidebook.lizards.page0.name: Lurking Lizard
book.pastel.guidebook.divinity.page0.tex:
I received major buffs to all major attributes.\
\
But I fear a terrible, close to irreversible cost, should I still die.
book.pastel.guidebook.boogaloo.oven.name: The Witch's Oven
book.pastel.guidebook.boogaloo.oven.page:
I never finished a furnace of my own. A Witch's Oven cooks just as well, and with a Clay Jar beside it, it also bottles the fumes coming off the food.\
\
[Jaramel](entry://general/jade_vines@jaramel) and [Broodfruit Popcorn](entry://cuisine/mermaids_popcorn) both come out of one.
book.pastel.guidebook.boogaloo.oven.ash_: Slush cooks down into Ash Flakes. Half the time the jar catches some Foul Fume as well.
book.pastel.guidebook.boogaloo.oven.bone: One chunk of Dragonbone takes ages, then gives me a whole pile of Bone Ash. Sometimes a Hint of Rebirth rises out of it.
book.pastel.guidebook.boogaloo.placer.fo: Once I've built the focus by hand, I can pack the whole structure into a single placer and put it down again wherever I like.
book.pastel.guidebook.boogaloo.placer.sh: The shrine packs up the same way. Handy when I want a second one somewhere else.
book.pastel.guidebook.boogaloo.placer.te: With an Onyx Pedestal in hand, the Temple folds into a placer too. That saves me a lot of crests and pillars.
book.pastel.guidebook.boogaloo.placer.en: The Enchanter's structure can be packed into a placer as well. It takes a bucket of Liquid Crystal to make.
book.pastel.guidebook.boogaloo.placer.pa: Even the biggest of them, with a Moonstone Pedestal at its heart.
book.pastel.guidebook.boogaloo.rainbow_s: Six Pigments, some sugar, corn syrup and a Uranium Nugget. Stirred into an Awkward Potion it brews a Chromatic Potion.
book.pastel.guidebook.boogaloo.attunemen:
Witches have their own word for what I do with color. They call it attunement.\
\
A Whiff of Magic over a bucket of lava on my [Pedestal](entry://general/pedestal), plus one color of powder, and out comes a humming gem. Each color gives a different one.
Cyan gives Attuned Topaz. A Distillery won't work without one.
Yellow gives Attuned Citrine. Every candelabra I make needs one.
Magenta gives Attuned Amethyst. Both the Tarot Deck and the Chalice ask for it.
Onyx needs the [Onyx Pedestal](entry://general/pedestal_upgrade_onyx) and black powder. The ritual for a Necromantic Stone won't start without it.
Moonstone takes a Breath of the Goddess instead of lava. Two of them go into an Eternal Catalyst, and one sits in each corner of a Werewolf Altar.
book.pastel.guidebook.boogaloo.pets.name: Pets
book.pastel.guidebook.boogaloo.pets.page: The little companions I keep in my pockets don't come from a crafting table any more. Mine all come off the Pedestal, each with a Breath of the Goddess worked in.
book.pastel.guidebook.boogaloo.pets.cmy: The plainer ones, like this Anvil, only need the [focus structure](entry://general/pedestal_upgrade_cmy).
book.pastel.guidebook.boogaloo.pets.onyx: The strange ones, like the Sun, the Moon or this Black Hole, want the [Onyx Pedestal](entry://general/pedestal_upgrade_onyx). The Black Hole even swallows a whole [Black Hole Chest](entry://magical_blocks/black_hole_chest).
book.pastel.guidebook.boogaloo.pigment.t: It doesn't have to be red. Every Truffalo Tuft crushes into two Pigment of its own color.
book.pastel.guidebook.boogaloo.fused_lif: The [Fusion Shrine](entry://general/fusion_shrine) doesn't only melt minerals together. With the right liquid in it, living things take new shapes too.
An Echo Shard and a Resonant Lily give me Chorus without a trip to the End.
This one works in plain water. A Nautilus Shell soaks up Moonstruck Nectar and Broodfruit until it glows.
Crossing the two deep blossoms gives me a sprouting [Jade Vine](entry://general/jade_vines) bulb without searching any ruins.
A Spectral Shard fused into a sapling. Whatever grows from it looks half dead, and I don't know why yet.
book.pastel.guidebook.boogaloo.foreign.p:
My Enchanter isn't picky about where an enchantment comes from. Once I've handled a few odd materials from a place, I can write its enchantments onto books here and upgrade them with Pigment, same as my own.\
\
A few I've used most:
book.pastel.guidebook.boogaloo.foreign.c: Queen Scales and Moonstone Cores, for something the ant worlds keep to themselves.
book.pastel.guidebook.boogaloo.foreign.f: Stratoshark Fins and feathers. Light Blue, of course.
book.pastel.guidebook.boogaloo.foreign.s: Keeps things I shoot from dropping. An Hourglass and a bit of Antimetal hold them still.
book.pastel.guidebook.boogaloo.foreign.x: A lens and some polymer plating. It sees right through things.
book.pastel.guidebook.boogaloo.foreign.u: Upgrading works just like it does for my own enchantments: the book, a pile of Pigment and plenty of experience.
book.pastel.guidebook.pastel_network_col: The more I got to grips with my Node Network, the more limitations I realised - especially when I wanted to use lots of nodes in a small space.\n\nThe fact that each node always has a random color was one of my... more interesting design decisions.
book.pastel.guidebook.provider_node.page: Make the items in the connected inventory available in their [Node Network](entry://pastel_network/pastel_network).\n\nItems are not pushed, but can be requested from [Gather Nodes](entry://pastel_network/gather_node) and [Buffer Nodes](entry://pastel_network/buffer_node).
book.pastel.guidebook.redstone_interacti: When I expose a [#](bb00bb)node[#]() to a [#](449900)redstone signal[#](), it loses the link to its attached inventory.

While the built-in redstone functionality of my [#](bb00bb)nodes[#]() is nice, certain situations have proven to require specialized control. The pure resources I recently learned about seem to have qualities suitable to such a task.
book.pastel.guidebook.tuning_stamp.page0:
An essential part of network management is being able to fine-tune where and how things go around. This crystal stamp allows me to manually add and remove nodes from networks.

[#](449900)Redo[#]() a preexisting connection to unlink it.
[#](449900)Shift-right-click[#]() to remove all connections.
